subject.title: Feature Request: Agent-triggered context compaction (self-compact tool)

question: Should OpenClaw expose a current-session-only model-callable self-compaction action through `session_status`, or keep compaction behind sender/control-plane authorization until a different policy gate exists?
rationale: Source inspection proves the API is missing, but the unresolved choice is a product/security boundary because the model would gain a new mutating action over active session context state.

options.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
options.body: Allow a current-session-only `session_status` compact action after the linked PR is refreshed and maintainer security/runtime proof is accepted.

options.title: Require Explicit Policy Gate
options.body: Keep the implementation direction but require an operator or tool-policy gate before exposing model-originated compaction.

options.title: Defer To Continuation Design
options.body: Pause the narrow action until maintainers decide whether broader continuation APIs should own voluntary compaction.

recommendation.title: Approve Narrow Self-Compaction
recommendation.body: Allow a current-session-only `session_status` compact action after the linked PR is refreshed and maintainer security/runtime proof is accepted.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across `session_status`, gateway/runtime surfaces, and compaction-adjacent behavior.
